sections.title: Official AWS Documentation, Whitepapers, and Blogs

entries.title: AWS Documentation
paragraphs: AWS publishes official documentation explaining its services, features, configurations, APIs, and recommended usage.
entries.recognitionCue: Need official technical information about an AWS service → AWS Documentation

entries.title: AWS Whitepapers
paragraphs: AWS whitepapers provide deeper guidance on architecture, security, cloud adoption, best practices, and Well-Architected design.

entries.title: AWS Blogs
paragraphs: AWS blogs contain announcements, technical explanations, architecture guidance, examples, and updates.
entries.memoryHook: AWS Blog = articles, updates, and guidance.

sections.title: AWS Prescriptive Guidance
paragraphs: AWS Prescriptive Guidance provides strategies, guides, and patterns for cloud projects and technical implementations.
sections.callout: How should we approach this? → AWS Prescriptive Guidance

sections.title: AWS Knowledge Center
paragraphs: The AWS Knowledge Center contains answers and troubleshooting guidance for common AWS technical questions.
sections.callout: Troubleshooting question, common AWS issue, or technical answer → AWS Knowledge Center

sections.title: AWS re:Post
paragraphs: AWS re:Post is an AWS community knowledge service where customers and experts can ask and answer technical questions.
sections.callout: Community technical question and answer → AWS re:Post

sections.title: Exam Trap — Documentation vs. Knowledge Center vs. re:Post
sections.callout: DOCUMENTATION = INSTRUCTIONS · KNOWLEDGE CENTER = ANSWERS · re:POST = COMMUNITY

sections.title: AWS Support
paragraphs: AWS provides different support options based on customer needs. The official CLF-C02 scope includes customer service and communities, AWS Developer Support, AWS Business Support, AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support, and AWS Enterprise Support. Different plans provide different levels of technical support, response, guidance, and business or enterprise assistance.
sections.callout: Match the workload's business criticality and support requirements to the AWS Support offering.

entries.title: AWS Developer Support
paragraphs: Developer Support is intended for customers developing and testing workloads who need technical support beyond basic customer service resources.

entries.title: AWS Business Support
paragraphs: Business Support provides broader technical assistance for customers operating business and production workloads.

entries.title: AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support
paragraphs: Enterprise On-Ramp provides an intermediate level of enterprise-oriented support for organizations that need enhanced assistance but may not require the highest enterprise support level.

entries.title: AWS Enterprise Support
paragraphs: Enterprise Support provides AWS's highest level of support for organizations with critical business workloads and extensive support requirements.

sections.title: Support Recognition Ladder
paragraphs: As business criticality and support requirements increase, the appropriate support offering changes. Do not memorize imaginary guarantees; match the scenario to the support level described by AWS.
sections.callout: DEVELOPER → BUSINESS → ENTERPRISE ON-RAMP → ENTERPRISE

sections.title: AWS Support Center
paragraphs: The AWS Support Center provides a location for managing support interactions with AWS.
sections.callout: Create or manage an AWS support case → AWS Support Center

sections.title: AWS Trusted Advisor
paragraphs: AWS Trusted Advisor analyzes AWS environments and provides recommendations. Its checks can address cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits or quotas.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company wants AWS recommendations for reducing unnecessary cost.
entries.recognitionCue: Recommendations, best-practice checks, or cost-optimization suggestions → AWS Trusted Advisor

sections.callout: TRUSTED ADVISOR = RECOMMENDATIONS

sections.title: AWS Health Dashboard
paragraphs: The AWS Health Dashboard provides information about AWS events that can affect customer resources and services.
sections.callout: AWS event affecting resources or service health relevant to a customer environment → AWS Health Dashboard

sections.title: AWS Health API
paragraphs: The AWS Health API provides programmatic access to AWS Health information.
sections.callout: Programmatically retrieve AWS Health events → AWS Health API

sections.title: Exam Trap — Trusted Advisor vs. AWS Health

table.caption: Separate improvement advice from current events
rows: What is happening to my environment?

sections.callout: ADVISOR = ADVICE · HEALTH = EVENTS

sections.title: AWS Trust and Safety
paragraphs: The AWS Trust and Safety team handles reports involving abuse of AWS resources, including AWS resources being used for abusive or prohibited activity.
sections.callout: Report abuse involving AWS resources → AWS Trust and Safety

sections.title: AWS Partner Network
paragraphs: The AWS Partner Network (APN) is the global community of AWS partners. Partners can include independent software vendors, system integrators, consulting organizations, and technology providers.
sections.callout: APN = AWS PARTNER ECOSYSTEM

sections.title: Independent Software Vendors
paragraphs: An independent software vendor (ISV) creates and sells software products.
sections.callout: ISV = BUILDS SOFTWARE

sections.title: System Integrators
paragraphs: System integrators help customers design, combine, implement, and operate technology solutions.
sections.callout: SYSTEM INTEGRATOR = PUT THE SOLUTION TOGETHER

sections.title: Exam Trap — ISV vs. System Integrator
sections.callout: ISV = SOFTWARE PRODUCT · SYSTEM INTEGRATOR = IMPLEMENTED SOLUTION

sections.title: Benefits of AWS Partnership
paragraphs: AWS supports a partner ecosystem around its cloud.
bullets: Potential volume discounts depending on program arrangements
sections.callout: Partners can gain skills, resources, community access, and eligible commercial benefits.

sections.title: AWS Marketplace
paragraphs: AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog where customers can find, purchase, deploy, and manage third-party software and services that run on AWS. Marketplace can also help with procurement, entitlements, governance, and cost management.
sections.callout: Find or buy third-party software for AWS → AWS Marketplace

sections.title: AWS Professional Services
paragraphs: AWS Professional Services provides expert assistance from AWS for cloud initiatives. This can involve large or complex transformation and implementation efforts.
sections.callout: Need AWS experts for a cloud project → AWS Professional Services

sections.title: AWS Solutions Architects
paragraphs: AWS solutions architects help customers understand and design architectures using AWS services.
sections.callout: Need architectural guidance → AWS solutions architect

sections.title: Exam Trap — Professional Services vs. Solutions Architect

table.caption: Keep the business need in mind

sections.callout: DESIGN HELP = SOLUTIONS ARCHITECT · PROJECT HELP = PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
